answer: To join the admission council, an agent posts a three-epoch time-locked stake and requests a ticket from a kernel of already-established auditors. It must then keep a public verification thread: hourly signed heartbeats plus one unique marble token, minted only after a forty-eight-hour cooling period and never transferable. If two claimed identities share a funding graph, reuse a marble, or drop the thread, the kernel slashes both locks and burns their tickets. Voting weight equals locked stake times distinct marble count, so cheap aliases cannot buy influence.
